BiblicalUsage: mârad is to rebel, and it runs through the history of Israel's kings. In 2 Chronicles 13:6 Jeroboam rebels against his lord Solomon's son, and in 2 Chronicles 36:13 Zedekiah rebels against Nebuchadnezzar, stiffening his neck and hardening his heart from turning to the LORD. In 2 Kings 18:7 Hezekiah rebels against the king of Assyria and prospers, and in 2 Kings 18:20 the Assyrian asks on whom Hezekiah trusts that he rebels. The word is the same act, blessed or cursed by whom it is against.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mârad shows me that rebellion is never a small thing. I hold that the stiff neck and the hardened heart are the same sin, whether against a king or against God.
